meta.title: States
meta.description: What the schedule shows while it waits, when it fails, and when there is nothing to show.

basics.intro: A schedule is rarely only full or only empty. loading and error are props you hold, and the component decides what that means for each view; the empty states follow from the items themselves.
points: Loading with nothing yet: a spinner, with the loading text for assistive technology.
Loading over data: the items stay visible and dimmed, and the region is marked aria-busy — a refresh never blanks the screen.
Error: a heading, the message you give, and a retry button when onRetry is set. It replaces the content, because a partial schedule is worse than none.
Empty: one text when no rendered shift holds an item, another inside a shift that is empty while others are not. The timeline keeps its grid and centers the message on it.
The loading state is announced once, not on every frame, and the busy marking is what tells a screen reader that the content is stale rather than gone.
The error state is a heading and text, not an alert that steals focus; the retry button is an ordinary button in the tab order.
An empty shift keeps its section and its heading, so the outline of the day does not change as items arrive.
renderEmpty, renderLoading and renderError replace the three; the parts emptyState, loadingState and errorState replace their markup.
The states carry no color of their own beyond the text tokens, so they follow the theme without being restyled.
There is one error at a time for the whole schedule; a per-shift error is not modelled.
The component never fetches, so it never decides on its own that it is loading: both props are yours.
Skeleton cards are not provided. The loading state is a spinner, or your own through renderLoading.
